subject: anatomy
title: Shoulder suspension, capsule and stabilizers
description: Shoulder stability depends on specific suspensory ligaments, cuff compression and capsular reinforcements. Joint cavities and adjacent bursae define routes for fluid spread.

subject: anatomy
title: Branch-level localization in the shoulder and arm
description: Selective muscle testing localizes a lesion along the brachial plexus or a terminal nerve. A lesion distal to an early motor branch can spare that muscle while affecting more distal targets.

subject: anatomy
title: Elbow stability and forearm load transfer
description: The radius and ulna function as a linked unit. The radial head, interosseous membrane and distal radioulnar stabilizers share longitudinal loads, while collateral ligaments control angular instability.

subject: anatomy
title: Forearm vessels and nerve relationships
description: Recurrent arteries reconnect distal vessels to the brachial system around the elbow. Fascial openings and muscle heads guide nerves into compartments and explain selective deficits.

subject: anatomy
title: Finger and thumb tendon mechanics
description: The extensor expansion, volar plates and flexor pulleys couple motion across finger joints. Their failure produces distinct deformities even when the main muscle and nerve remain intact.

subject: anatomy
title: Hand nerve branches, arches and tendon sheaths
description: Hand symptoms depend on whether a lesion affects proximal or distal branches, and infections follow specific synovial sheaths. Palmar arches and tendon nutrient folds occupy different depths.

subject: anatomy
title: Hip capsule, cartilage and communicating spaces
description: The capsule has asymmetric femoral attachments and contains the capital growth plate. The acetabular articular ring, central fossa and adjacent bursae explain loading and fluid distribution.

subject: anatomy
title: Thigh circulation and changing neurovascular planes
description: The profunda femoris and its perforating branches form longitudinal collateral channels, while the femoral vein changes sides along the artery. Superficial venous and cutaneous nerve routes explain selective procedural deficits.

subject: anatomy
title: Knee recesses, stabilizers and load-bearing mechanics
description: Knee fluid follows synovial recesses, while flexion changes cruciate tension, patellar restraint and the muscular work required to support body weight.

subject: anatomy
title: Localizing leg nerve lesions by spared functions
description: Distinguish nerve injury levels by combining cutaneous loss with motor functions supplied before and after the suspected lesion.

subject: anatomy
title: Ankle mortise, tendon restraints and surgical relations
description: The ankle mortise accommodates the asymmetric talar trochlea; retinacula restrain tendons along different routes from the collateral ligaments.

subject: anatomy
title: Foot arches, intrinsic mechanics and deep circulation
description: Passive fascial tension and intrinsic muscle lines of pull shape the foot as a lever, while plantar nerve branches and vascular arches occupy distinct tissue planes.

subject: embryology
title: Limb growth, compartment innervation and developmental disruptions
description: Limb elongation, muscle innervation and congenital deformities arise through different developmental processes. Distinguishing loss of growth, altered pattern and reduced fetal movement clarifies otherwise similar limb findings.

subject: histology
title: Cartilage resilience and bone mechanobiology
description: Limb tissues share connective-tissue ancestry but have distinct nutrient routes and mechanical components. Cartilage hydration, osteocyte sensing and osteoclast resorption explain functional and disease patterns.

subject: histology
title: Muscle force transmission, excitation architecture and repair
description: A skeletal muscle is a mechanically continuous tissue whose fibers transmit force through collagen. Sarcomeric accessory proteins, triads and satellite cells solve distinct structural problems.

subject: physiology
title: Skeletal-muscle length, load, activation and relaxation
description: Separating active from passive tension, force from shortening, and electrical excitation from calcium handling explains muscle behavior under experimental and limb-loading conditions.
